name: CapitalNumbers Infotech Limited
sector: Digital engineering and outsourced enterprise software services
summary: Cash-generating services with substantial financial assets and a completed acquisition, but recent core-profit decline, modest organic momentum and mixed capital allocation. The linked asset-plus-operating model supports a value thesis at the dated quote, not a proven compounder; liquidity and deployment discipline remain important constraints.
identity_note: BSE code 544343 and ISIN confirmed in September 2026 holdings. Listed 27 January 2025 per the issuer’s primary results certificate. NSE interoperability records do not turn this into an NSE listing. [S7][S11][S91]

score_note: Full canonical arithmetic; no caps. IAS is conditional on the 19 October 2026 secondary quote, ₹5 lakh reference size and the explicit asset/operating model. Display rounding must not alter the unrounded classification.

gates.reason: IPO/OFS expense allocation was corrected and seller recovery documented; capital-allocation and presentation concerns limit stewardship confidence without proving deliberate diversion.

Unmodified audited statements support current asset/earnings analysis. Original/restated cash-flow classifications and bounded gratuity/dividend text inconsistencies are disclosed rather than treated as a fabricated reconciliation.

No funded debt; acquisition and operating uses are covered by the reviewed asset pool under principal and severe linked models. Clear means no material funding obstacle identified, not a guarantee of unrestricted cash or future solvency.

Official lot400 and 60 observed secondary sessions support conditional reference capacity. Current BSE restrictions, two-sided depth and spreads remain to be checked; no blanket surveillance clearance.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
CapitalNumbers is an asset-backed, mixed-quality services watchlist candidate rather than an evidence-backed compounder. The ₹73.19 secondary close on 19 October 2026 implies ₹178.78 crore equity, compared with ₹171.34 crore of March bank/deposit/investment assets before the subsequently completed Epitome acquisition and other cash uses. That comparison is not a current cash balance or liquidation floor. FY2026 operating sales rose 5.34%, but strict core pre-tax earnings fell 16.38%; investment income supported reported profit. The completed annual model separates those two economics and funds the acquisition, working capital, capex and dividends without new debt in all principal scenarios. It does not assume IPO earmarks are unavailable for their authorized uses. [S1][S2][S8][S9][S90]

BQS 5.46, Growth Quality GQS 5.20 and conditional IAS 7.165 map to a speculative or mixed-quality watchlist, not a buy instruction. The base dated total-return IRR is 33.49% to 31 March 2031, but this is an assumption-dependent result driven partly by realization and retention of financial assets. Severe linked operating, investment and capital-allocation stress produces ₹30.56 terminal value and −17.84% annualized return. No portfolio allocation is inferred from the ₹5 lakh liquidity reference.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Cutoff: 20 October 2026. Legal identity is CapitalNumbers Infotech Limited, ISIN INE0WXM01011, BSE code 544343, BSE SME listing on 27 January 2025. The 30 September filing explicitly identifies SME status, 24,426,990 issued shares, no outstanding ESOPs, warrants or convertibles, and no disclosed promoter pledge, non-disposal undertaking or other encumbrance. Promoter/group ownership is 74.98% across four holders; public ownership is 25.02% across 4,377 holders. These are dated declarations, not continuous assurance. [S7][S11]

The primary history comprises original FY2021 audited group accounts, prospectus-restated FY2022–24 and audited FY2025–26 consolidated accounts. Accounting bases are retained rather than silently spliced. Current FY2027 interim operating cash and target audited profit/net assets are unavailable. G1 Integrity and G2 Reliability are Conditional because corrected IPO expense allocation and bounded presentation/basis issues deserve monitoring; no evidenced diversion or modified audit opinion is inferred. G3 Funding is Clear on the reviewed asset/obligation evidence and modeled stress, not a guarantee. G4 Tradability is Conditional: dated secondary activity and official lot size support a capacity estimate, but current BSE restrictions, spread, depth and executable two-sided markets need a live check. Overall confidence is Medium, with price/liquidity and forecasts explicitly conditional. [S1][S3][S7][S8][S90][S91]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 6, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 6, BAL 8, EXEC 5 and EARN 3. All have at least Medium evidence confidence; projected growth does not inflate REV. The chosen five-year FY2021–26 revenue CAGR is 17.43%, starting REV 7; the maximum one-point downward trajectory adjustment reflects the sustained FY2024–26 slowdown, giving REV 6. Three-year CAGR 4.30% is shown as contrary evidence, not substituted to choose a preferred score. The purchase of Epitome occurred after the historical window. [S1][S3][S4][S12]

BQS = .20×5 + .20×5 + .12×6 + .10×5 + .12×5 + .10×6 + .08×8 + .08×5 =5.46. GQS = .40×6 + .20×5 + .15×3 + .15×5 + .10×6 =5.20. IAS reuses Q=5.46 exactly: .25×5.46 + .35×10 + .20×6 + .10×8 + .10×3 =7.165. R10 follows base IRR 33.49% minus the 15% nominal-INR equity hurdle, a spread 18.49 percentage points. D6 reflects survival but meaningful permanent-loss stress; P8 reflects conservative valuation sensitivities rather than a catalyst bonus; L3 follows the greater-than-ten-day capacity band. Coverage is 100% and no numerical override is applied. Scores are research assessments, conditional on the dated reference price and position, not probabilities or execution clearance.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company sells digital engineering, outsourced development and enterprise software services, not a subscription product with verified recurring ARR. Management describes FY2026 revenue as 91% time-and-materials, with 250-plus clients,500-plus professionals and AI services above 10%. Geographic revenue mix is approximately US 41%, Europe/UK 31%, Middle East 11%, India 10% and other 7%. These are management disclosures; their sum does not independently verify customer economics. Delivery is employee/subcontractor intensive, so utilization, bill rates, attrition and selling efficiency matter more than physical capacity alone. [S5][S15]

Epitome adds Salesforce implementation/managed services, CPQ, contract-lifecycle and enterprise-workflow capabilities across Conga, Agiloft and Onit. The July SPA describes 100% ownership for approximately ₹40 crore cash, subject to net-working-capital and other agreed adjustments. ₹23.4 crore was paid in August and the 25 August release confirms completion. The remaining approximately ₹16.6 crore is therefore a consideration/timing issue, not evidence that control never transferred. Audited target earnings, acquired net assets and the full adjustment schedule have not been located, so they are not invented. [S2][S9][S10]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Historical profitability and a diversified client base support useful delivery relationships, but not a structural monopoly. Prospectus top-ten client concentration declined from 30.75% in FY2022 to 26.78% in FY2023,25.68% in FY2024 and 24.12% in the half-year to September 2024. The latest concentration table is older than the valuation date. Management’s approximately 90% retention and 10% normal churn describe relationships, not a contracted revenue annuity. Skills, certifications and platform partnerships aid access but can be replicated; generative AI can both increase demand for implementation and reduce billable effort. MOAT 5 recognizes contestable relationships without mistaking lack of exceptional barriers for missing knowledge. [S3][S5]

InfoBeans is a useful operating comparator because of digital engineering and enterprise-platform work, but is materially larger: audited FY2026 revenue ₹513.57 crore versus ₹394.78 crore, PAT ₹86.66 crore versus ₹37.97 crore. Its strict other-income-excluded EBITDA proxy is ₹112.65 crore, about 21.93% of sales, close enough to make CapitalNumbers’22% reference EBITDA margin plausible rather than guaranteed. InfoBeans’ prior acquisition impairment ₹23.38 crore and deferred-consideration reversal ₹22.12 crore also illustrate why gross acquisition economics must be inspected instead of relying on a net exceptional line. Different scale, accounting and customer mix prevent an automatic peer multiple. No stale IPO-date peer P/E is presented as current. [S13]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Audited/restated group operating revenue in ₹crore is 47.0411,69.0718,92.5723,98.1721,99.7290 and 105.0497 for FY2021 through FY2026. Five-year CAGR 17.43% contrasts with three-year 4.30%; the latest annual additions are ₹23.5005, ₹5.5998, ₹1.5569 and ₹5.3207 crore from FY2023 onward. This is a real early scaling record followed by a pronounced slowdown, not continuous high growth. Original FY2020 comparative revenue ₹29.4310 crore provides context but is not used to extend a six-observation five-year formula incorrectly. [S1][S3][S4][S12]

The June 2026 call’s minimum 35% FY2027 combined-growth ambition includes acquisition revenue and new-business wins before normal churn. Prior FY2026 organic guidance of about 15% was not delivered; actual growth was 5.34%, with management attributing delays to enterprise contracting and ramp-up. Epitome’s disclosed standalone turnover was US$3.281880m, US$4.116898m andUS$2.867087m in CY2023/24/25, a 30.36% decline in the latest year. Neither acquired growth nor target recovery is treated as organic proof. The model assumes 8% annual legacy growth in base and a first full acquired year ₹25.8 crore, explicitly an analyst INR run-rate assumption below management’s ₹28–30 crore discussion, not an audited translation or forecast. [S5][S6][S9]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Core growth quality is mixed. The strict operating proxy subtracts all other income from PBT and retains bank/other non-debt finance costs: FY2026 ₹23.5089 crore versus FY2025 ₹28.1122 crore. At a consistent assumed 25% tax rate, core NOPAT is ₹17.6317 crore versus ₹21.0842 crore. FY2026 reported profit therefore does not establish organic profit growth. Staff, sales, software and platform capabilities provide runway, but the economic test is incremental core cash profit, not the size of the addressable technology market. [S1][S5]

The reproducible funding-side capital proxy is equity plus funded debt minus cash, deposits and investments. It rises from ₹11.1546 crore in FY2021 to ₹15.0490 crore in FY2023 and ₹20.2071 crore in FY2026. Five-year incremental core-NOPAT/capital is 61.87%, while the three-year proxy is 7.69%, below the 12–18% nominal-INR hurdle range. FY2026 average operating-capital return is 85.58%, but excluding the IPO-funded financial portfolio makes that figure unsuitable as a return on all shareholder money; full committed-capital core return is about 10.12%. One-year incremental capital falls, so that ratio is NM. These proxies retain tax/employee balances and differ from project IRRs; old asset utilization and expensed human capital matter. CAP 5 reflects the strong early cohort, weak recent incremental result and unproven acquisition deployment, not an invented neutral score. [S1][S3][S4][S12]

The remaining March IPO technology and business-development budgets, about ₹27.89 crore combined, mainly authorize staffing/selling/program costs. The prospectus technology object includes substantial HR expenditure, so charging the entire budget again as physical capex would double-count operating costs. Forecast margins include those expenses; separately modeled physical/development cash totals ₹11.2 crore over five years in base. The ₹40 crore acquisition is paid once and includes estimated acquired working capital, with adjustment sensitivity. [S3][S7][S8] The three-year operating-capital increase of ₹5.1581 crore comprises a ₹0.9666 crore reduction in PPE/development and a ₹6.1247 crore rise in residual operating/tax/employee balances. Cash capex ₹4.3204 crore less depreciation ₹4.5928 crore is not identical to the asset movement because disposals and historical noncash/basis changes also matter. The full exact asset roll-forward is not claimed; these are capital-efficiency cross-checks, not project IRRs. [S1][S3][S4]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
The statutory auditor’s unmodified opinion includes emphasis on gross IPO/OFS expenses originally charged against company securities premium. The selling-shareholder portion was recovered on 24 November 2025; FY2026 cash flow and securities premium both record a net ₹11.3451 crore recovery. The use-of-proceeds certificate’s gross ₹11.4022 crore figure differs by ₹0.0571 crore; that gross-to-net residual is not falsely reconciled. This is an evidenced accounting/allocation correction, not a conclusion of deliberate diversion. The correction is positive contrary evidence, while the original error and subsequent object revision limit a high stewardship score. [S1][S7][S17]

The 1 October filing confirms shareholder approval on 29 September: the original ₹5 crore subsidiary object was broadened to Epitome/entities, and ₹11.4646 crore unused issue-expense budget was reallocated toward the acquisition. This removes the earlier pending-approval question. The September 2028 object-use timeline is not a reason to ignore the August control completion. IPO earmarks are within bank/deposit assets, not additional money or automatically legally pledged cash. In FY2024 the company bought back 23,910 pre-bonus shares at ₹6,216, with about ₹18.3192 crore total cash including buyback tax; the later IPO raised fresh money and provided equal-size OFS liquidity. That capital-allocation cycle requires scrutiny but alone is not misconduct. [S3][S7][S8][S10]

The 18 July 2026 secretarial audit reports compliance and adequate processes, with a secretary transition in May 2025. Annual RPT disclosures include remuneration of ₹0.51 crore to Mukul Gupta, ₹0.45 crore to Herprit Gupta and ₹0.564 crore to the CFO, plus ₹2.2506 crore to the employee gratuity trust. These disclosed commercial/employment items do not themselves establish abusive related-party conduct. September holdings report no promoter encumbrance and no dilution claims. EXEC 5 balances the missed organic guidance against the completed acquisition milestone; integration returns are still unproven. [S1][S5][S6][S11]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The FY2024 original owners’ PAT ₹26.1307 crore reconciles to prospectus-restated ₹25.9887 crore through FX+₹0.0433, tax-interest+₹0.0260, current-tax−₹0.0299, deferred-tax+₹0.0649 and removal of prior-period credit−₹0.2463 crore. The financial-history artifact preserves the older original and restated cash-flow presentations: FY2024 CFO ₹22.3401 versus ₹19.4876 crore, with deposit/finance classifications also differing in investing/financing. The remaining full cash-flow bridge is not claimed resolved. Both bases are cash-positive; current liquidity is not dependent on selecting the more favorable one. [S3][S4]

FY2022–26 cumulative CFO ₹87.4044 crore divided by consolidated PAT ₹110.4791 crore is 0.791×; cash capex totals ₹6.7956 crore. That warning is investigated rather than automatically excused: interest and investment-sale gains enter profit but are excluded from CFO, while cash tax covers total profit. FY2026 CFO ₹17.1399 crore less physical/development capex ₹0.8135 crore leaves reported FCF ₹16.3264 crore. Other income ₹10.5459 crore includes bank interest ₹5.6107 crore and realized investment-sale profit ₹4.7334 crore. It is not all unrealized, but neither is it recurring services EBIT. The strict core EBITDA proxy is ₹25.0980 crore,23.89% of operating revenue, not management’s roughly 31% EBITDA/total-income measure that includes treasury income. [S1][S3][S4][S5]

Receivables rose from ₹6.4170 crore to ₹10.2257 crore while sales grew 5.34%; approximately ₹1.9707 crore is over one year old. Unbilled revenue ₹1.7579 crore is separate and not added twice. The year’s ₹2.1445 crore FX/derivative expense versus ₹0.5068 crore previously includes a ₹1.095 crore derivative liability; all FX costs are not assumed to disappear. Other expenses increased ₹7.3819 crore, including marketing, technical consultants, rent and software, while employee expense rose ₹2.4191 crore. Margin compression has an operating source. [S1]

The gratuity note’s ‘unfunded’ wording and a−₹2.2506 crore line labeled past-service cost conflict with the disclosed contribution/plan-asset bridge. Net liability reconciles as ₹3.4331+₹0.7505−₹2.2506−₹0.2324=₹1.7006 crore: this is a cash funding contribution, not an inferred profit reversal. Audit prose also says no dividend was paid while directors’ disclosures and cash flow identify the December 2025 interim dividend ₹2.4427 crore. These bounded presentation issues warrant correction, not an unsupported fraud allegation. FY2026 audit-trail testing reports operation and no tampering found; contingent-liability/commitment notes are nil at March, before the subsequent acquisition. [S1]

March financial assets comprise cash/bank ₹88.6192 crore, long deposits ₹1.6003 crore and investments ₹81.125 crore. The portfolio includes funds, bonds/equities and ₹0.2506 crore bitcoin; it is not all risk-free cash. A 5% investment realization haircut is in base and 25%/50% in stress. Government advances, broker balances and FD interest are identified separately. The model does not add March property value, goodwill, IPO earmarks or the already received OFS reimbursement on top of the same capital again. [S1][S7] The standalone balance sheet places ₹87.9746 crore of cash/bank balances and the same ₹81.125 crore current-investment portfolio at the parent, versus group cash/bank ₹88.6192 crore. This limits, but does not eliminate, a foreign cash-access concern. Opening net tax payable ₹0.037 crore is settled once within the modeled ₹2.1048 crore employee/tax provisions. Government-authority advances ₹3.4084 crore stay within the broad working-capital bridge and are not separately recovered again. [S1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
The dated quote gives reported P/E7.01×, strict core-PAT proxy P/E10.14× and reported FCF yield 9.13%. These are cross-checks, not intrinsic values. March financial assets less the full ₹40 crore acquisition, pre-entry final dividend ₹2.442699 crore and separately settled derivative/employee/tax claims ₹3.1998 crore give a static ₹125.7020 crore financial-asset bridge before later operations or market changes, about ₹51.46 per share. It is not observed October cash. The shareholder register supports 2.442699 crore diluted shares with no current claims. [S1][S2][S9][S11][S90]

The annual model covers FY2027–31 from audited March opening assets; investor entry is 19 October 2026 and exit 31 March 2031, about 4.45 years, not a mislabeled five-year investor CAGR. Unreported April–October operations are forecast, not known actuals. Base legacy growth 8%, acquired sales ₹17/25.8/27.348/29.53584/31.89871 crore, EBITDA margins 22%/18%, broad working capital 13% of revenue, cash capex ₹2/2/2.2/2.4/2.6 crore and depreciation ₹1.7/1.8/1.9/2/2.1 crore are explicit assumptions. Acquired opening WC is included within consideration and removed from the incremental operating funding calculation. All original acquisition cash is deducted once, including August’s payment. Bank/deposit assets and 95% of investment book value fund the purchase and operations; no new debt or equity is needed. [S1][S2][S9]

Treasury earns an assumed 4% pre-tax cash yield on a cash-use-adjusted pool, taxed 25%; this income is excluded from exit business EBIT. Terminal equity adds retained cash once. Hypothetical future ₹1 per-share annual dividends are deducted from cash and included in dated IRR; the FY2026 final dividend belongs to the earlier record-date holder and is never credited to the new buyer. At 10× exit EBIT, base terminal price ₹254.73 and IRR 33.49% result. Bear ₹95.89/6.26% and bull ₹473.37/53.17% are conditional outcomes, not expected probabilities. All three fully fund their annual modeled uses. [S1][S11][S90]

The margin 18/22/26% × exit 6/10/14× two-way grid gives 21.98%–44.16% IRR. Zero acquired profit gives 29.69%;25% investment haircut 32.59%; extra ₹40 crore acquisition with no added profit 31.26%;22% WC 32.73%;₹40 crore unavailable bank assets 31.22%;5% entry execution cost 32.00%. At 12/15/18% hurdles, conditional entry-price thresholds are ₹157.74/140.46/125.46, not executable buy limits. A reverse model with base target/asset assumptions meets 15% even with legacy contraction; at 6× exit EBIT the implied legacy growth threshold is−9.76% annually. This apparent cushion depends critically on asset realization and disciplined deployment, not proof that contraction is harmless. The severe combined case below is more informative than any single favorable multiple. [S1][S9][S90] The 1 October voting-results filing confirms that the AGM resolutions, including the ₹1 final dividend, passed; this supports treating the pre-entry record-date distribution as an existing cash obligation. [S14]

Opening-claim closure: the existing ₹2.1048 crore year-1 payment comprises ₹0.4042 crore current provisions (net tax ₹0.0370 and leave ₹0.3672) plus ₹1.7006 crore net noncurrent gratuity. The latter is an explicit full-funding contribution assumption, not a statement that employees are immediately entitled to that payout. The model already pays it, so no terminal deduction is added. Plan assets ₹2.2467 crore are already netted against the obligation and are not added to treasury. Future employee-benefit costs are cash-funded within operating expenses; no duplicated benefit payment or tax deduction is introduced. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The ordinary bear combines 10% initial legacy contraction, weak subsequent growth,8% acquired EBITDA margin,14% legacy margin,22% working-capital intensity, ₹45 crore acquisition cost,25% investment haircut, impairment of the ₹1.9707 crore aged receivable balance and 6× exit EBIT. Terminal ₹95.89 remains above the dated entry, but only because financial assets and continuing earnings survive. That result is not a guaranteed downside floor. Receivable impairment is noncash: recoverable opening WC falls, impairment is deducted from PAT and added back to CFO, and replacement working capital is funded once. [S1][S9][S90]

A more severe linked case lowers legacy margin to 8%, acquired margin to zero, realizes only 50% of investment book value, raises WC to 30%, spends an additional ₹40 crore without added profit and applies 4× exit EBIT. Terminal value falls to ₹30.56, about 58.25% below entry, with−17.84% annualized return. Minimum modeled cash remains about ₹31.00 crore and no new borrowing is needed, so this is mainly permanent loss of owner value rather than a modeled rescue-financing case. More extreme fraud, inaccessible assets or undisclosed claims are not assigned invented probabilities. The most important falsifier is failure to reconcile the post-acquisition financial-asset pool and its permitted uses. [S1][S7][S8]

Strong positive historical operating cash, no funded debt and corrected OFS recovery are the best evidence against a pure value-trap interpretation. Conversely, the market may already understand slowing legacy growth, treasury-heavy profit, the target’s latest revenue decline and SME execution constraints. No informational edge or imminent rerating is asserted.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At the dated quote and unchanged 2.442699 crore shares,5× and 10× prices require ₹893.91 crore and ₹1,787.81 crore equity value. Using the base terminal cash only as a conditional bridge,10× EBIT and 20% EBIT margin imply revenue about ₹323.84/770.79 crore, corresponding to 25.25%/48.97% business revenue CAGR over FY2026–31. Required incremental WC at 13% is about ₹28.91/87.01 crore above the opening proxy, before additional capacity, development or acquisitions. That reverse arithmetic is not a self-funding forecast: higher growth cannot inherit base cash without paying its own capital needs. [S1][S11][S90]

The completed base reaches ₹186.25 crore revenue and 3.48× the dated price, while bull reaches ₹256.92 crore and 6.47× through 15% legacy growth, stronger margins and 14× exit EBIT. The bull’s 5× outcome is possible but demanding, not demonstrated by current organic momentum;10× is unsupported by the completed scenarios. The investor horizon to March 2031 is shorter than five years, while operating growth is measured from March 2026. No accessible market-share percentage is invented without a reliable denominator.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Review the next published half-year and annual filings, not a fabricated quarterly cash-flow series. First, reconcile financial assets after the ₹23.4 crore payment and remaining consideration; a reduction not explained by approved acquisitions, operating investment, dividends or market changes is a thesis-break investigation. Second, require the target’s consolidated revenue, operating profit, cash and final purchase-price allocation; another material decline from CY2025 US$2.867m or new adjustment above the ₹40–45 crore modeled range warrants rerunning the model. Third, separate legacy growth from acquisition contribution; two more comparable half-years near the recent low-single-digit trend invalidate the 8% reference path unless another evidenced driver appears. [S1][S2][S5][S9]

Fourth, monitor strict core margin against FY2026 23.89% EBITDA and the 22% base; sustained movement toward 18% triggers the lower-margin grid, not an automatic allegation. Fifth, track receivables ₹10.2257 crore, aged-over-one-year ₹1.9707 crore and unbilled ₹1.7579 crore; growing ageing with weaker collections triggers the impairment/WC stress. Sixth, verify the remaining IPO objects and recovery disclosures against actual cash uses, without adding earmarks as new capital. Seventh, track options/new issues, promoter encumbrance and ownership changes from September’s no-claim/no-encumbrance baseline. Eighth, recheck current BSE lot, restrictions, bid/ask depth and 20/60-session capacity before any implementation; a one-sided market overrides a smooth theoretical liquidation estimate. [S1][S7][S8][S11][S90][S91]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Classification: speculative or mixed-quality watchlist, with an asset-backed value thesis and material quality limitations. It does not satisfy the compounder criteria: BQS 5.46 and GQS 5.20 are below the required levels, and several operating/stewardship factors remain ordinary. The modeled return is attractive relative to a 15% hurdle, but IAS 7.165 does not overcome the distinction between a useful valuation case and a high-quality reinvestment engine. No governance, funding or persistent cash-quality numerical override is applied. [S1][S3][S7][S9]

Action is research-priority/watchlist, conditional on confirmation of post-acquisition asset realization and actual tradeability. At the ₹5 lakh reference position,400-share lots cost ₹29,276 at the dated quote;17 lots total ₹497,692. Using the more conservative 60-session low×volume mean/median proxy gives 10.62 days at 5% participation,26.55 days at 2% and 5.31 days at 10%. The 20-session version is 12.42/31.06/6.21 days. All 60 sessions have provider observations, so no missing-day zero fill is required, but low×volume is only a turnover bound and cannot establish spread or order-book depth. L3 is a conditional capacity assessment, not suitable position sizing or an order recommendation. [S90][S91]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary issuer annual reports, prospectus, use-of-proceeds certificate, SPA/completion/payment filings and the September holdings underpin the review. FY2021 scanned P&L, balance sheet and cash flow were visually checked; FY2022–24 restated figures are identified separately from later original comparisons. InfoBeans is a limited operating cross-check, not a complete current peer valuation. The quote and OHLCV history are secondary and dated 19 October 2026; the intake CSV has no verified date and is not used as current. [S1][S3][S4][S7][S9][S11][S12][S13][S90]

Open evidence includes final acquisition adjustments/payment dates, audited target profit/net assets, current group cash/investment realizable value and any legal restrictions, updated customer concentration, a fully reconciled older cash-flow reclassification, and live BSE surveillance/spread/depth. These gaps bound confidence and implementation; they do not erase the completed cash, debt, dividend and equity calculations. Forecast growth, margins,25% tax, treasury returns, asset haircuts, acquired WC, old-provision settlement timing, future dividends and exit multiples are analyst assumptions. Annual source balances remain distinct from those estimates. The model and financial-history artifacts retain full arithmetic, original inputs and sensitivities; no scenario is represented as a promised return.

GOV.reason: Corrected OFS expense allocation and subsequent approval are positive remediation, but original process weakness and capital-allocation cycle prevent a high stewardship score. No deliberate abuse is inferred.

MOAT.reason: Diversified relationships and profitable delivery are useful but contestable. T&M services, replicable platform skills and churn do not establish exceptional barriers.

REV.reason: Five-year comparable 17.43% starts at 7; sustained recent slowdown warrants the permitted one-point downward adjustment to 6. Three-year 4.30% is disclosed; acquisition forecasts are excluded.

DUR.reason: Enterprise-platform and AI-related services provide accessible demand, but churn, competitive pricing and technology-driven reductions in billable effort constrain durability.

CAP.reason: Strong early scaling and five-year incremental 61.87% coexist with recent three-year 7.69%, full-capital return 10.12% and unproven new acquisition deployment. Mixed economics support 5 rather than NS.

CASH.reason: Positive multi-year CFO and low physical capex support realization, but raw 0.791 conversion, rising/aged receivables and cash-flow classification differences prevent a strong-band score. Treasury tax/classification is explicitly analyzed.

BAL.reason: Large reviewed financial assets and no funded debt cover the acquisition and all modeled stress uses; severe modeled minimum cash remains about ₹31 crore. Asset availability/market risk prevents exceptional assurance.

EXEC.reason: Meaningful acquisition closing delivered, but recent organic guidance missed and integration returns are not established. Mixed delivery supports 5.

EARN.reason: Core operating profit declined while higher bank interest and realized investment-sale gains supported reported earnings; per-share profit also diluted by the full-year IPO share base.

R.reason: Base dated IRR 33.4915% less fixed 15% hurdle gives 18.4915 percentage points, meeting canonical R10. Conditional asset realization and complete linked sensitivities are disclosed.

D.reason: Principal bear remains funded, but severe combined capital-allocation and operating stress loses 58.25% of the dated price. Survival does not eliminate permanent-loss risk.

P.reason: Lower 18% legacy margin and 6× exit EBIT still exceed the 15% hurdle in the two-way grid; asset realization/deployment, not heroic market share, drives the cushion. Combined severe stress still fails.

L.reason: Conservative 60-session turnover proxy implies 10.62 days at 5% participation, lower score 3 in the>10–20 day band. Secondary data and unknown current depth/restrictions keep this conditional.

Q.reason: Final BQS reused exactly, with no separate GQS or cash-quality re-addition.

ranking_eligibility.reason: Complete supported factors and linked annual model; IAS comparison remains conditional on the stated dated quote and reference-position assumptions, not execution clearance.

notes: March 2026 assets are an audited opening, not an observed October NAV. FY2027 includes unreported April–October operating forecasts and the already completed acquisition cash use.
The full acquisition price is deducted once, including the August payment. IPO earmarks are included in bank assets and are not added again or treated as legally frozen.

Opening investment haircut is a valuation adjustment to opening assets. Receivable impairment is noncash, deducted from profit and added back to CFO; opening recoverable working capital is reduced before funding its forecast target.

Working capital is a broad cash requirement proxy retaining government advances and statutory balances; derivative liability is excluded and settled separately. Existing employee/tax provisions are paid once; future operating costs cover new employee obligations.

Future operating margins include staff, selling and program expenses. The remaining IPO technology/business budgets mainly authorize operating spending; they are not charged again as capex. Physical and software-development cash is separately modeled.

Treasury cash returns are taxed separately and retained only once. Exit business value excludes treasury income; terminal cash is added once. Future dividends are deducted from cash and included in dated investor cash flows. The pre-entry FY2026 final dividend is deducted but never credited to the new investor.

Acquired opening working capital is estimated at the scenario working-capital ratio times the first full-year target revenue. It is included within acquisition consideration, not funded twice through operating cash flow; no acquired asset value is added to terminal equity separately.

No outstanding dilution claims were disclosed in September 2026 holdings. Future equity issuance is not assumed. Any modeled new debt remains conditional and charges full-opening plus half-year draw interest.
No transaction probabilities or guaranteed price targets. Personal tax excluded; execution sensitivity is explicit.

cash_conversion_FY22_26.note: Restated FY22–24 plus annual FY25–26. FY24 CFO includes different deposit/finance classifications from the later original comparative. Treasury income is excluded from CFO while tax covers total earnings; raw conversion is not pure core conversion.

FY24_basis_bridge.note: Profit reconciliation closes exactly. Cash-flow classification differs; the full residual is not claimed resolved or fabricated. Current solvency is not dependent on this difference.

capital_cross_check.note: Capital increase is predominantly non-PPE working/tax/employee balances, not the annual capex budget. Net capex minus depreciation is−.2724crore; asset disposals, historical restatement/FX and noncash differences explain why it is not identical to−.9666crore closing asset change. Exact full asset reconciliation is not asserted. No acquisition capital was paid before the March2026 endpoint; full40crore purchase is modeled subsequently.

scope_and_limits: Strict core removes all other income and retains all finance costs, including non-debt bank/derivative costs. It is a conservative EBIT/NOPAT proxy, not a statutory operating subtotal. A 25% normalized tax assumption is used consistently.

Funding-side operating capital excludes cash, deposits and investments but retains other tax/employee/net operating balances. It is not a clean project-IRR denominator. Deposits and original-versus-restated history differences are explicit.

The five-year incremental proxy includes profitable early scaling; the three-year proxy exposes recent operating stagnation. FY2026 one-year capital change is negative, so incremental ROIC is NM, not exceptionally positive.

Full committed-capital return includes idle IPO assets to avoid rewarding exclusion of shareholder-funded cash. The Epitome acquisition is post-March2026 and is included in the forecast acquisition bridge, not these historical returns.

Separate gross margin, clean maintenance capex, recurring lease liability and FY2027 interim cash flow are not available as reliable standardized measures. Rent remains operating expense. Do not combine standalone cash with group profit.
